text: According to the valence bond theory the hybridization of central metal atom is dsp$^{2}$ for which one of the following compounds?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ni ($Z=28$) is $[\text{Ar}]3d^{8}4s^{2}$. $dsp^{2}$ hybridisation needs one vacant $3d$ orbital, which a $3d^{8}$ ion gets only when a strong field ligand pairs its electrons.

(A) $\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{2}\cdot 6\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$: six-coordinate $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{8}$) with weak field ligands undergoes no pairing and uses $4s$, $4p$ and $4d$ orbitals: $sp^{3}d^{2}$, octahedral.


[IMG]

(B) $\mathrm{K}{}_{2}[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]$: in $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$, $x+4(-1)=-2$ gives $x=+2$, so Ni is $3d^{8}$. The strong field ligand $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ pairs the eight electrons into four $3d$ orbitals, and the vacant $3d$, $4s$ and two $4p$ orbitals give $dsp^{2}$, square planar.


[IMG]

(C) $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{0}$ with the strong field ligand CO becomes $3d^{10}4s^{0}$, so $4s$ and $4p$ give $sp^{3}$, tetrahedral.


[IMG]

(D) $\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{8}$) with the weak field ligand $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ undergoes no pairing, so $4s$ and $4p$ give $sp^{3}$, tetrahedral.


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: The correct order of intensity of colors of the compounds is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In all three complexes nickel is $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{8}$), and the colour comes from absorption of visible light by d–d transitions; the colour is intense when the absorption is strong and lies well inside the visible region.

$[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$ is tetrahedral with the weak-field ligand $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$: the small splitting keeps the absorption inside the visible region, and the absence of a centre of symmetry makes its d–d transitions only partly forbidden, so it absorbs strongly and is intensely coloured.

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$ is octahedral and centrosymmetric, so its d–d transitions are Laporte-forbidden and weak; it is only pale green.

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$ is square planar (also centrosymmetric) with the strong-field ligand $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$: the large splitting pushes its absorption towards the violet and ultraviolet, so it is the least coloured (pale yellow).

The order of intensity of colour is therefore $[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}>[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}>[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: The species given below that does NOT show disproportionation reaction is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A species can disproportionate only when its central atom is in an intermediate oxidation state, so that it can be oxidised and reduced at the same time.

Oxidation state of Br: $\mathrm{BrO}{}_{4}{}^{-}$ $+7$, $\mathrm{BrO}{}^{-}$ $+1$, $\mathrm{BrO}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ $+3$, $\mathrm{BrO}{}_{3}{}^{-}$ $+5$.

In $\mathrm{BrO}{}_{4}{}^{-}$, bromine is already in its highest oxidation state ($+7$), so it cannot be oxidised further and can only be reduced; it cannot disproportionate. In the other three ions, Br lies between $-1$ and $+7$, so they can disproportionate.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: An inorganic Compound 'X' on treatment with concentrated $H_{2}SO_{4}$ produces brown fumes and gives dark brown ring with FeSO$_{4}$ in presence of concentrated $H_{2}SO_{4}$. Also Compound 'X' gives precipitate 'Y', when its solution in dilute HCl is treated with $H_{2}S$ gas. The precipitate 'Y' on treatment with concentrated HNO$_{3}$ followed by excess of $NH_{4}OH$ further gives deep blue coloured solution, Compound 'X' is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Brown fumes of $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ with conc. $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ and the brown ring with $\mathrm{FeSO}{}_{4}$ in conc. $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ identify the anion as nitrate, which rules out $\mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}){}_{2}$:

$4~\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}{}^{-}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}\longrightarrow 4\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}↑+\mathrm{O}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

$\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}{}^{-}+3\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}+4\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\longrightarrow \mathrm{NO}+3\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O},[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}+\mathrm{NO}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{5}(\mathrm{NO})]{}^{2+}_{\mathrm{brown}\mathrm{ring}}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

A precipitate with $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{S}$ in dilute HCl means a group II cation; $\mathrm{Co}{}^{2+}$ belongs to group IV and is not precipitated here, so $\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ is ruled out.

Of the group II cations left, only copper gives a deep blue colour; black $\mathrm{CuS}$ (Y) dissolves in conc. $\mathrm{HNO}{}_{3}$ and excess $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$ forms the tetraammine complex, whereas $\mathrm{Pb}{}^{2+}$ gives only a white precipitate of $\mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{OH}){}_{2}$ with $\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{OH}$.

$3~\mathrm{CuS}+8\mathrm{HNO}{}_{3}\longrightarrow 3\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}){}_{2}+2\mathrm{NO}+3\mathrm{S}+4\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

$\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}+4\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}\longrightarrow [\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}]{}^{2+}_{\mathrm{deep}\mathrm{blue}}$

So X is $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}){}_{2}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text:

Which among the above compound/s does/do not form Silver mirror when treated with Tollen's reagent?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror with aldehydes, including compounds that change into an aldehyde in the basic reagent; ketones do not react.

(I) 2-Methylpropanal is an aldehyde, so it gives a silver mirror.

(II) Prop-1-en-2-ol is the enol of acetone; it tautomerises to $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$, a ketone, so no silver mirror forms.

(III) Cyclohexylidenemethanol is the enol of cyclohexanecarbaldehyde; tautomerisation gives an aldehyde, so it gives a silver mirror.

(IV) Tetrahydropyran-2-ol is a cyclic hemiacetal; in the basic reagent it opens to 5-hydroxypentanal, which is oxidised, so it gives a silver mirror.


[IMG]

Only (II) does not form a silver mirror.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text:
250 mL of 0.5 M NaOH was added to 500 mL of 1 M HCl. The number of unreacted HCl molecules in the solution after complete reaction is $___________$ $\times$ $10^{21}. ($Nearest integer)

$(N_{A} = 6.022$ $\times$ $10^{23})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know that, number of moles $= V_{L}$ $\times$ molarity and number of millimoles $= V_{mL}$ $\times$ molarity

So, millimoles of NaOH = 250 $\times$ 0.5 = 125

Millimoles of HCl = 500 $\times$ 1 = 500

Now, reaction is


[IMG]

125 millimoles of NaOH reacts with 125 millimoles of HCl. So, millimoles of HCl left = 375

Moles of HCl = 375 $\times$ $10^{-3}$

Number of HCl molecules 

= Avogadro's constant $(N_{A})$ $\times$ moles of HCl

= 6.022 $\times$ $10^{23}$ $\times$ 375 $\times$ $10^{-3}$

= 225.8 $\times$ $10^{21} = 226$ $\times$ $10^{21}$

Therefore, answer is 226.

text:
The spin-only magnetic moment value for the complex [$Co(CN)_{6}$]$^{4-}$ is $__________ BM ($nearest integer).

[At. no. of Co = 27]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[$Co(CN)_{6}$]$^{4-}$

x + 6 $\times$ ($-$1) = $-$4

where, x, 6, $-$1 and $-$4 are the oxidation number of Co, number of CN ligands, charge on one CN and charge on complex.

$x = +2, i.e. Co^{2+}$

Electronic configuration of $Co^{2+}$ : [Ar]$3d^{7}$ and $CN^{-}$ is a strong field ligand which can pair electron of central atom.

 
[IMG]

It has one unpaired electron (n) in 4d-subshell.

So, spin only magnetic moment ($μ$) = $\sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM = $\sqrt{1(1+2)}$ BM = $\sqrt{3}$ BM

where, n = number of unpaired electrons

$μ$ = $\sqrt{3}$ BM = 1.73 BM

Nearest integer = 2

text:
$2SO_{2}(g) + O_{2}(g)$ $⇌$ $2SO_{3}(g)$

In an equilibrium mixture, the partial pressures are 

$P_{SO3} = 43$ kPa; $P_{O2} = 530 Pa$ and $P_{SO2} = 45$ kPa. The equilibrium constant $K_{P} = ___________$ $\times$ $10^{-2}. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
On reaction, $2SO_{2}(g) + O_{2}(g)$ $\to$ $2SO_{3}(g)$

Given values are : $p_{SO3} = 43$ kPa, $p_{O2} = 530 Pa = 0.53$ kPa

$p_{SO2} = 45$ kPa

Now, $K_{p}=\frac{[p_{SO3(g)}]^{2}}{[p_{SO2(g)}]^{2}\times [p_{O2}]}$

On putting given values, we get

$\Rightarrow K_{p}=\frac{(43)^{2}}{(45)^{2}\times 0.53}$

$=\frac{1849}{2025\times 0.53}=\frac{1849}{1073.25}$

$=1.7228$

$=\frac{1.7228\times 10^{2}}{10^{2}}=172.28\times 10^{-2}=172$

Hence, the equilibrium constant, $K_{p} = 172$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text:
The inactivation rate of a viral preparation is proportional to the amount of virus. In the first minute after preparation, 10% of the virus is inactivated. The rate constant for viral inactivation is $___________$ $\times$ $10^{-3} \min ^{-1}. ($Nearest integer)

[Use : ln 10 = 2.303; $\log _{10} 3 = 0.477$; property 
of logarithm : $\log  x^{y} = y \log  x$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Unit of rate constant is $\min ^{-1}$, so it must be a first order reaction. For first order reaction,

k $\times$ t = 2.303 log$\frac{A_{0}}{A_{t}}$

k is the rate constant

 t is the time

 $A_{0}$ is the initial conc. 

$A_{t}$ is the conc. at time, t

Using formula,

$A_{0} = 100, A_{t} = 90$ in 1 min

So, K $\times$ 1 = 2.303 $\times$ log$\frac{100}{90}$

= 2.303 $\times$ (log 10 $-$ 2 log 3)

= 2.303 $\times$ (1 $-$ 2 $\times$ 0.477)

= 0.10593

= 105.93 $\times$ $10^{-3}$

$\approx$ 106

Hence, the rate constant for viral inactivation is 106.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift

text: At 20${}^{\circ }$ C, the vapour pressure of benzene is 70 torr and that of methyl benzene is 20 torr. The mole fraction of benzene in the vapour phase at 20${}^{\circ }$C above an equimolar mixture of benzene and methyl benzene is $_____________$ $\times$ $10^{-2}. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Vapour pressure of pure benzene, $p_{A}^{o}$ = 70 Torr

Vapour pressure of pure methyl benzene, $p_{B}^{o}$ = 20 Torr

This mixture is equimolar, so number of moles of benzene, 

$n_{A} =$ number of moles of methyl benzene, $n_{B}$

Mole fraction of benzene in vapour phase, $y_{A} =$ $\frac{p_{A}}{p_{T}}$ .... (i)

where $p_{A}$ is pressure of benzene in mixture.

$p_{A}=p_{A}^{o}χ_{A}_{Molefraction}=p_{A}^{o}\times \frac{n_{A}}{n_{A}+n_{B}}=p_{A}^{o}\times \frac{n_{A}}{2n_{A}}=\frac{p_{A}^{o}}{2}$

$p_{T}$ is total pressure,

$p_{T}=p_{A}^{o}χ_{A}+p_{B}^{o}χ_{B}=p_{A}+p_{B}$ (pressure of methyl benzene)

$p_{T}=\frac{p_{A}^{o}}{2}+\frac{p_{B}^{o}}{2}=\frac{p_{A}^{o}+p_{B}^{o}}{2}$

Putting in above equation (i),

$y_{A}=\frac{\frac{70}{2}}{\frac{(70+20)}{2}}=\frac{70}{90}$

$y_{A} = 0.78 = 78$ $\times$ $10^{-2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Morning Shift
